subject.title: [Feature]: Feishu Group Chat SubAgents for User-Specific Skills and Memory

question: Should Feishu group chats get first-class opt-in dynamic per-sender agents, or should OpenClaw keep sender-scoped group sessions plus explicit subagent/thread commands as the supported isolation model?
rationale: Current source has partial session and subagent infrastructure, but the requested architecture changes channel routing, agent lifecycle, memory isolation, skills, config writes, resource limits, and shared-group security boundaries.

options.title: Design generic contract first
options.body: Create a generic admin-authorized identity-to-agent lifecycle and memory contract, then let Feishu implement it as one channel owner surface.

options.title: Keep session-only routing
options.body: Keep current groupSessionScope and explicit subagent/thread mechanisms, documenting that full per-user agent orchestration belongs in an external plugin or deployment pattern for now.

options.title: Defer To Narrower API Work
options.body: Resolve account-scoped group sessions, channel threading policy, and user skill preferences before revisiting automatic Feishu group subagents.

recommendation.title: Design generic contract first
recommendation.body: Create a generic admin-authorized identity-to-agent lifecycle and memory contract, then let Feishu implement it as one channel owner surface.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the strongest current-main history signal across Feishu dynamic-agent routing and related session/subagent behavior.
